data.name: Hw.Diag.Intro
data.value: Measures latency to the router and the internet, packet loss, DNS and speed. It takes about 25 seconds and uses your connection, capped at about 350 MB of data. Nothing is written to disk.

data.name: Hw.Diag.Servers
data.value: Talks only to the router, to 1.1.1.1, to 1.0.0.1 and to speed.cloudflare.com, over HTTPS.

data.name: Hw.Diag.Failed
data.value: The test did not finish. The log has the details.

data.name: Hw.Diag.Stage.Latency
data.value: Measuring latency and packet loss (about 7 s)…

data.name: Hw.Diag.Finding.AllGood
data.value: Low latency, no packet loss and no sign of bufferbloat. If the game still stutters, the connection is probably not the cause: check the Bottleneck page and the temperatures.

data.name: Hw.Diag.Finding.RouterUnstable
data.value: The local network is unstable (router: {0} ms, {1}% loss, {2} ms jitter). If you are on Wi-Fi, move closer to the router or use a cable.

data.name: Hw.Diag.Finding.RouterSilent
data.value: The router does not answer ping (some models block it). That alone is not a problem.

data.name: Hw.Diag.Finding.InternetUnreachable
data.value: None of the internet servers answered: no internet access, or ping is blocked by the network.

data.name: Hw.Diag.Finding.InternetLossLocal
data.value: There is packet loss to the internet ({0}%). It probably comes from the local network.

data.name: Hw.Diag.Finding.InternetLossProvider
data.value: There is packet loss to the internet ({0}%). Since the router is fine, the problem is likely the line or the provider.

data.name: Hw.Diag.Finding.HighLatencyLocal
data.value: High latency to the internet ({0} ms).

data.name: Hw.Diag.Finding.HighLatencyProvider
data.value: High latency to the internet ({0} ms). The router answers well, so the delay comes from the provider.

data.name: Hw.Diag.Finding.HighJitter
data.value: Jitter is high ({0} ms): latency fluctuates, which causes stutter in online games.

data.name: Hw.Diag.Finding.Bufferbloat
data.value: Latency climbs to {0} ms when the connection is saturated (bufferbloat). Enable SQM/QoS on the router or cap the speed at about 90%.

data.name: Hw.Diag.Finding.SlowDns
data.value: DNS took {0} ms. Switching to a public resolver such as 1.1.1.1 can speed up page loads.

data.name: Hw.Diag.Finding.LowDownload
data.value: Low download speed ({0} Mbps) for games, streaming and updates.

data.name: Bench.Cpu.Description
data.value: Path tracing of a 3D scene, on the same principle as Cinebench. The scene and the workload are always the same, so the score is comparable between runs.

data.name: Bench.Cpu.Result.RatioNote
data.value: How much multi-core gains over single-core depends on the {0} physical cores and on SMT.

data.name: Bench.Sim.Description
data.value: How many frames per second the CPU sustains in a 30,000-unit simulation: physics, collision, AI and draw preparation.

data.name: Bench.Sim.Result.Note
data.value: The score is the median of 3 passes. Workers stay on physical cores so the result varies less between runs.

data.name: Bench.Memory.Description
data.value: RAM latency and bandwidth (read and copy), outside the processor cache.

data.name: Bench.Memory.Result.Note
data.value: The history score is the read bandwidth. The test needs about 2.5 GB free and gives it all back when done.

data.name: Bench.Loading.Description
data.value: Simulates loading a game: one large pack and many small files, read from disk without the Windows cache.

data.name: Bench.Loading.Result.Note
data.value: The score is the map time: lower is better. Test files live in a temporary folder and are deleted at the end.

data.name: Bench.Disk.Description
data.value: Sequential 1 MB reads and writes and random 4 KB accesses with a real queue (1, 8 and 32 requests at once), CrystalDiskMark style.

data.name: Bench.Disk.Result.Note
data.value: Score version 2, with a real I/O queue. Not comparable with ResetExplode's, which used 8 synchronous threads.
